nodes.label: Photosynthesis
nodes.summary: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy.

nodes.label: Chloroplasts
nodes.summary: Chloroplasts are specialized leaf organelles containing chlorophyll that absorb light to power photosynthesis.

nodes.label: Light-Dependent Reactions
nodes.summary: Occurring in thylakoid membranes, these reactions split water to release oxygen and produce ATP and NADPH.

nodes.label: Calvin Cycle
nodes.summary: Taking place in the stroma, the Calvin cycle uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide into three-carbon sugars.

nodes.label: Stomata
nodes.summary: Stomata are small leaf pores that absorb carbon dioxide while balancing oxygen and water vapor loss.

nodes.label: Global Ecological Impact
nodes.summary: Photosynthesis supplies atmospheric oxygen and forms the base of most global food chains.
